chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the grandfather, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not find anyone who has spoken regarding it except by his own opinion, except for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May Allah perfect you, so what did the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say regarding it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When it is tomorrow, meet me until I make you read it in a book.' I said: 'May Allah perfect you, narrate to me, for your hadith is more beloved to me than you making me read it in a book.' So he said to me for the second time: 'Listen to what I am saying to you. When it is tomorrow, meet me until I make you read it in a book.'

So I went to him the next day after the noon prayer, and it was my time when I would be alone with him, between the noon and afternoon prayers. I disliked asking him except when alone, out of fear that he would issue a verdict to me due to the presence of others, through dissimulation (taqiyyah). So when I entered upon him, he turned to his son Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'Make Zurara read the Parchment of the Inheritance Shares.' Then he arose to sleep.

So I and Ja'far (peace be upon him) remained in the room. He stood up and brought me a parchment like the thigh of a camel, and said: 'I will not make you read it until you make Allah a guarantee upon you that you will not narrate to anyone what you read in it, ever, until I permit you' — and he did not say 'until my father permits you'. I said: 'May Allah perfect you, and why do you restrict me, and your father did not command you with that?' He said to me: 'You will not look in it except upon what I have said to you.' I said: 'So that is for you.' And I was a man knowledgeable about the inheritance shares and bequests, perceptive of them, and calculating them. I had waited a long time seeking something cast to me from the inheritance shares and bequests that I did not know, so I could not attain it.

So when he cast towards me a side of the parchment, it was a thick book, recognizable as being from the books of the predecessors. So I looked into it, and found in it the opposite of what was in the hands of the people regarding the close relative (al-silah) and enjoining good, which has no difference [in common knowledge], and the generality of it was like that. So I read it until I reached its end, with a bad self (thoughts), little retention, and a sick opinion, and I said while reading it: 'Falsehood,' until I reached its end. Then I folded it and handed it to him.

So when morning came, I met Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'Did you read the Parchment of the Inheritance Shares?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'How did you view what you read?' I said: 'Falsehood, it is nothing; it is the opposite of what the people are upon.' He said: 'So that which you saw, by Allah, O Zurara, is the truth. That which you saw was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and written by Ali (peace be upon him) by his own hand.'

So Satan came to me and whispered in my chest, saying: 'And what makes him know that it was dictated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and written by Ali (peace be upon him) by his own hand?' He said to me before I spoke: 'O Zurara, do not let Satan make you doubt. By Allah, you have doubted.' I said: 'And how can I not know that it is the dictation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the writing of Ali (peace be upon him) by his own hand, and my father narrated to me from my grandfather that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) narrated that to him?'

He said: 'I said: No, how (can I doubt)? May Allah make me a ransom for you.' And I regretted what had escaped me from the book, and if I had read it while I knew it, I would have hoped that not a single letter of it would have escaped me.

Umar ibn Udhaynah said: 'I said to Zurara: Indeed, some people have narrated to me from him and from his father (peace be upon him) matters regarding the inheritance shares, so I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say: This is false; and whatever of them is true, say: This is true, and do not narrate it and remain silent.' So I narrated to him what Muhammad ibn Muslim had narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the daughter and the father, and the daughter and the mother, and the daughter and the two parents. So he said: 'It is, by Allah, the truth.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.إِمْلَاءُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Dictation of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation (concealment of belief/rulings due to fear)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Shia inheritance rulings according to the narration of Zurara?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia concept of 'Sahifa al-Faraid,' a preserved parchment of inheritance rulings attributed to Ali ibn Abi Talib, which the Imam Muhammad al-Baqir presented to Zurara to resolve discrepancies with Sunni jurisprudence. The narrative underscores the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving the Prophet's original legal teachings, with the Imam cautioning Zurara against public dissemination to avoid political persecution (Taqiyya) while affirming the text's divine origin.
